text: In the Beginner project, you built Overlook Medical Group's backup and restore plan, and that plan already exists — it isn't revisited here. This project starts from a completely different kind of ticket: the database is up, backups are fine, and people are complaining it's slow.

Two emails land the same week. Billing says invoice lookups have been crawling all week, every morning, with patients on hold. Scheduling says the appointment calendar freezes for whole minutes around mid-morning, and they can't book patients fast enough. Neither email mentions the other department. Each one assumes the problem is specific to their own screen.

But both complaints point back to the same one shared Azure SQL Database, OverlookClinicalDB. dbo dot Invoices is Billing's table, one row per invoice. dbo dot Appointments is Scheduling's table, one row per scheduled visit. Both departments also join back to the same shared dbo dot Patients and dbo dot Providers reference tables.

That overlap is exactly why this chapter treats two complaints as one investigation instead of two unrelated tickets. Same database, same shared tables, and both emails mention roughly the same mid-morning window, when the clinic is busiest and both departments are hitting the database hardest at once.

This chapter is a performance-tuning project, not a backup project. You'll query what's actually running with DMVs, read real execution plans, fix a missing index, untangle a blocking chain, automate maintenance so the fixes stick, and later diagnose a second, unrelated slowdown. Next lesson: turning these two vague complaints into one concrete diagnostic plan.
